result.title: Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE): Fine-grained Hallucination Detection for LLMs from Embeddings
result.summary: Hallucination detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world deployments. While recent works, such as Semantic Entropy (SE) and Kernel Language Entropy (KLE), identify hallucinations by measuring semantic disagreement across multiple generated responses using Natural Language Inference (NLI) models, these methods depend on separately loaded NLI classifiers to estimate pairwise semantic similarity, introducing significant computational overhead. We propose Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE), a variant of Kernel Language Entropy (KLE) that replaces its NLI-derived semantic graph with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel applied to dense sentence embeddings generated by a BGE embedding model, while retaining KLE's graph Laplacian, heat kernel, and von Neumann entropy formulation unchanged. By computing similarities directly in a continuous embedding space, the proposed method provides a symmetric and computationally efficient alternative to NLI-based semantic comparison. We evaluate our approach across 30 experimental setups (covering multiple question-answer datasets and open-weight LLM families) using both AUROC and AUARC, and demonstrate that this RBF-based method achieves competitive hallucination detection performance against state-of-the-art methods.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 EGKE，把 KLE 中基于 NLI 的语义图替换为 BGE 句嵌入上的 RBF 核，保留图拉普拉斯、热核与 von Neumann 熵框架，用于 LLM 幻觉检测，并在 30 组问答数据集与开源模型设置上用 AUROC/AUARC 评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用嵌入空间相似图上的熵度量生成样本间语义分歧，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹间相似度刻画与 STOP/置信判断提供可核查的线索；但对象是文本输出分布而非内部推理状态，且不涉及视觉，联系较间接。
